svg.text: Sixteen techniques, ordered by how much they ask of you. Read top to bottom: obligation falls, cost rises.
Before any of them, encode the invariant in the type when you can. Otherwise a test along inbound → interior → outbound earns its keep.
Any function with non-trivial logic: branches, loops,
Every deployable unit. The app boots and answers.
low power, catches the embarrassing failures
After every bug fix; the failing test comes first.
Reimplementing a known algorithm against a trusted reference.
Unit tests lean on mocks for an external service.
HTTP endpoints, CLI workflows, a platform-specific runtime.
Code calls third-party APIs: LLM, payments, auth.
Refactoring legacy code with no test suite to lean on.
a Golden test on unknown behaviour
CLI commands, plugin hooks, or config described in docs.
Critical modules; or coverage is high yet bugs still escape.
UI work where exact pixel layout is the contract.
When a 2× slowdown would itself be a user-visible bug.

bug-catching power, from the skill’s cost-benefit table. Teal depth tracks the tier. Italic notes name a technique’s nearest relative or the boundary it guards. Full triggers and costs: references/test-types.md
